blocks.text: Luke names particular people and groups in the events leading to Jesus’ death: Judas, chief priests, scribes, temple captains, elders, the arresting group, and those who mock him. The wider passion narrative distributes responsibility among different actors rather than assigning it to Jewish people as a whole. Nothing in this account supports collective Jewish guilt or the charge of deicide.

Several details in this chapter invite careful reading. Ancient witnesses differ over whether Luke 22:19b-20 includes the longer wording about the second cup and the new covenant, and they also differ over the angel and Jesus’ agony in verses 43-44; the textual questions remain debated. The description of rulers called “Benefactors” has also been read alongside the violent ruler in Luke’s minas parable, with readers differing over whether that ruler represents God directly, exposes domination, or functions through contrast. Finally, the instruction to buy swords is immediately followed by the disciples’ attempted sword use, Jesus’ rejection of it, and his healing of the injured man. The sequence therefore cannot be used to authorize religious violence.
